reuse.why: Extends the existing getScheduledAmount, but re-implements the 7.5% tolerance inline instead of calling getApproxNumberThreshold from #shared/rules.

duplication.why: The approximate-tolerance formula is copied from getApproxNumberThreshold, and the rangeRounding parameter is kept as dead code alongside the new rule.

placement.why: The rule sits in the shared helper as it should, but the operator that selects it is only supplied by the API model, so the planning paths (forecast, preview, posting, rule-action sync, templates) never reach the approximate branch.

scope.why: Edits are limited to the helper, the API model and tests, though the API test and helper comments describe different rules.

maintainability.why: A positional four-argument helper with a parameter neutralised by `void rangeRounding`, a default op of 'isbetween', and an approximate rule that applies only where callers remember to pass the op is hard to own.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount computes Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075) itself instead of getApproxNumberThreshold; forecast-schedules.ts, schedules/app.ts (updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule), computeSchedulePreviewTransactions and schedule-template.ts call the helper without the op.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts: getApproxNumberThreshold's body inlined as a local `tolerance` instead of calling the shared function.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gained an amountOp parameter with an isapprox branch while keeping the now-dead rangeRounding parameter; forecast normalizeSchedule, updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions and the budget template call it without the op, so only api-models.ts gets the approximate rule.
